topic: CallDiff 2026: Diffs for Function Call Stacks Across Git Commits

key_points: Primary tool under review. CLI that diffs call stacks across git commits — 'like git diff, but for who-calls-whom'.
Built for agentic code review: when an agent rewires call flow, plain line diffs bury the shape of the change; calldiff shows which callees appeared, disappeared, or moved under an entrypoint.
Supports 22 languages via AST/tree-sitter (TypeScript, TSX, JavaScript, JSX, Python, Go, Rust, Java, Ruby, C, C++, C#, PHP, Kotlin, Swift, Scala, Lua, Elixir, Bash, Haskell, Zig, Solidity, OCaml).

Three commands: `diff` (git-diff shaped, `-`=gone from 'from', `+`=new in 'to'), `tree` (plain ASCII call tree, needs --entry), `reach` (all call paths from one symbol to another, needs --entry and --to).
Output: colored ASCII callstack trees by default; `--format json|yaml|md|jsonl` for agents/scripts.
Built on the incur CLI framework (wevm/incur): `skills add`, `mcp add`, `--llms`, CTAs after diffs, typed flags.
Install via `npx calldiff@latest` or `npm install -g calldiff`. MIT license. TypeScript. 296 stars, 14 forks at research time (2026-08-11).
Syntactic (AST-based) not a full typechecker — dynamic calls won't resolve. Grammars install on first use into ~/.cache/calldiff/grammars (override with CALLDIFF_GRAMMAR_CACHE).
Prompts users/agents: 'dearest clod, walk me through the code changes you made using npx calldiff@latest'.
Closest direct competitor: structural call-graph diff tool for multi-language codebases, built to work with coding agents.
Instead of a line diff, codiff shows what changed at the function level: functions added/modified/removed with call relationships mapped across files.
No LLM, no embeddings, fully offline.
Currently only 2 languages: Python (.py), TypeScript (.ts, .tsx) — much narrower than calldiff's 22.
Install via `pip install codiff`; `codiff diff` compares working tree to HEAD, or `--base`/`--head` for two refs.
Supports `--format mermaid` for PR-description diagrams.
Ships a GitHub Action (codiff-action on GitHub Marketplace). 7 stars at research time. Python. Created 2026-06-16.
Jackson Gabbard's widely-cited 'Stacked Diffs Versus Pull Requests' post — the canonical piece on why diff-shaped workflows (Phabricator) beat PR-shaped ones for review.
Argues engineers who used Phabricator's stacked-diff workflow love it and seek it out; those who only use GitHub PRs don't understand the fuss.
Heavily discussed on Hacker News (HN item 18119570 and 26922633) — evidence of sustained developer interest in diff-centric review.
Context: call-stack diffs are an extension of the same 'shape-of-the-change' idea, applied to the call graph rather than file layout.
DZone article on building call graphs for code exploration using Tree-sitter — the underlying technique both calldiff and codiff rely on.
Tree-sitter provides fast, incremental, error-tolerant parsing across many languages, which makes AST-based call-graph extraction practical and multi-language.
Establishes the technical foundation for the category (AST-based, not runtime/profiler-based call graphs).
CLI framework calldiff is built on. 594 stars at research time, TypeScript.
Purpose: 'CLI framework for agents and humans' — provides skills add, mcp add, --llms output, typed flags, and CTAs (call-to-actions) after diffs.
Signals calldiff is designed for AI-agent consumption, not just human CLI use.

stats.fact: calldiff supports 22 languages (TypeScript, Python, Go, Rust, Java, C/C++, C#, Ruby, PHP, Kotlin, Swift, Scala, Lua, Elixir, Bash, Haskell, Zig, Solidity, OCaml, JS/JSX/TSX) via tree-sitter AST parsing.
calldiff was created 2026-08-07 and had 296 stars / 14 forks as of 2026-08-11, with the most recent push on 2026-08-11.
calldiff is MIT-licensed and written in TypeScript; installable via `npx calldiff@latest` or `npm install -g calldiff`.

calldiff exposes three commands: diff (git-diff shaped), tree (ASCII call tree, requires --entry), and reach (call paths from one symbol to another, requires --entry and --to), plus --format json|yaml|md|jsonl for agents.
calldiff's main competitor codiff supports only 2 languages (Python and TypeScript) and 7 stars, vs calldiff's 22 languages and 296 stars.
calldiff is built on the incur CLI framework (wevm/incur), which has 594 GitHub stars and provides agent-oriented features: skills add, mcp add, --llms, and CTAs.
calldiff's Show HN post (Show HN: Calldiff – a CLI to see callstack diffs in all major languages) appeared on Hacker News with 2 points and 0 comments at research time.

The stacked-diff workflow that calldiff extends is well-established: Graphite's 'Show HN: Stacked Diffs on GitHub' drew 159 points and 64 comments on HN; 'Stacked Diffs versus Pull Requests' drew 104 points and 73 comments.
calldiff's parsing is syntactic (AST-based via tree-sitter), not a full typechecker — dynamic calls will not resolve; grammars install on first use into ~/.cache/calldiff/grammars.

angles: Position calldiff as the call-graph answer to the agentic-code-review problem: plain line diffs bury the shape of an agent's rewiring, and call-stack diffs surface which callees appeared, disappeared, or moved.
Lead with the 22-language breadth as the differentiator vs codiff's 2 languages — that's the single strongest objective advantage to feature.
Highlight the agent-first design: --format json/yaml/md/jsonl, --llms, skills add / mcp add, built on incur — this tool is built to be consumed by AI agents, not just humans.
Compare diff semantics head-to-head: calldiff's git-diff-shaped `diff`, `tree` (call tree), and `reach` (call-path search) vs codiff's function-level add/modify/remove + Mermaid output.
Practical review walkthrough: install via npx, run `calldiff diff main feature`, read the ASCII call-tree diff to verify an agent rewired call flow as claimed.
Call out the honest limitation: AST-based means dynamic/dispatch calls won't resolve, and entrypoint inference only catches exported functions whose expanded trees changed.
Frame the 'shape-of-the-change' philosophy: same insight as stacked diffs (review the change shape, not the file diff), applied to the call graph.
Agentic-review workflow: paste 'dearest clod, walk me through the code changes you made using npx calldiff@latest' to get a call-flow walkthrough from an agent.
